strengths: Clear problem motivation with effective intuition (Figure 1) for why dynamic target selection overcomes static augmentation limitations
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4+ benchmark suites (D4RL, OGBench, navigation, manipulation) with best/near-best on 16/18 datasets
Particularly strong results on navigation tasks (AntMaze +8.7 over DiffuserLite) and generalization to severe OOD scenarios (Table 3: 36.7 when baselines fail)
Thorough ablation studies clearly demonstrating component contributions, including comparison with random targets and pseudo-target strategy justification
Rigorous distribution shift experiments (Tables 2-3) showing practical generalization beyond training distribution
Honest computational analysis with practical solutions (periodic planning reduces 4× overhead by 77% with minimal performance loss)
Excellent reproducibility with detailed algorithms, hyperparameters, implementation details, and promised code release
Visualization validation (Figure 4) demonstrating retrieved targets are reasonable and reachable in practice
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing components (standard retrieval, heuristic target selection, existing diffusion models) without significant methodological innovation
Fundamental limitation acknowledged but unsolved: method depends on high-return state coverage in dataset; becomes ineffective when such states are absent

Inconsistent improvements: marginal gains on Medium-Expert datasets (~1-3%) and performance degradation vs. MOPO on HalfCheetah under distribution shift, suggesting method doesn't universally improve generalization

Ad-hoc design choices lack principled justification: selection of longest-remaining-trajectory criterion (Eq. 4) is intuitive but arbitrary; classification vs. regression for step estimation not empirically compared
Significant computational overhead: 4× inference time increase per step (0.06s→0.26s in AntMaze); periodic replanning adds implementation complexity and is not always practical
Return value computation underspecified: unclear how discounted returns are computed in practice, especially critical for sparse-reward navigation tasks where return differentiation is unclear
Narrow experimental scope: all evaluations on D4RL/OGBench synthetic environments; no real robotic or domain-specific offline RL applications tested
Step Estimation module details sparse: inverse dynamics model training procedure not described; potential for error propagation not addressed; classification formulation not compared to alternatives
Training-testing mismatch: random offset during training (Eq. 12) vs. fixed offset during testing could impact generalization; stability of gradient term ∇J_ϕ not discussed
